purpose: The dashboard layout — a reflowing grid of tiles with no breakpoints for a caller to get wrong.

useInstead.when: the children belong in one column, one after another
useInstead.use: Stack — is this a grid of peers, or a sequence?
the child on its own — a one-item grid is a wrapper with no job

useInstead.when: the content is tabular, with shared columns and a header
useInstead.use: a table — a grid of cards cannot align columns or be sorted

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for Grid decisions in this package.
decision.beforeTheRules: The default `columns="auto"` is right almost always. Reach for a fixed count only when the layout genuinely breaks without one.

rules.if: you are laying out dashboard tiles, stat cards or any set of peers
rules.because: auto-fit reflows by item width, so it adapts at every viewport with no media query — a fixed column count is the single commonest way a generated dashboard breaks on a narrow screen

rules.if: the layout is meaningless at any other count — a two-up comparison, a paired before/after
rules.because: it still collapses to one column below the mobile breakpoint rather than overflowing

rules.if: you want narrower or wider tiles
rules.then: override --shell-grid-min-item, do not switch to a fixed count
rules.because: the minimum item width is what auto-fit reflows against; tuning it keeps the responsive behaviour
it defaults to the same 16px rhythm as <main> and every other container, which is what makes pages look consistent

constraints: Tracks are minmax(0, 1fr), so a long unbroken string cannot push the grid wider than its container.
Grid does not set margins on its children. Spacing between tiles is the gap, always.

composition.childrenContract: Tiles — usually Card, but any element. Each child becomes one grid cell.
composition.notes: Do not wrap children in extra divs to control spacing; the gap already handles it and a wrapper introduces a level the gap cannot reach.

antiPatterns.dont: Setting columns={3} for a dashboard because the design shows three across
antiPatterns.why: the design shows three across at ONE width; auto gives you three there and fewer where three would not fit

antiPatterns.dont: Adding margin-bottom to cards inside a Grid
antiPatterns.why: margin adds to the gap, so the rhythm becomes 16px in one place and 28px in another

antiPatterns.dont: Nesting a Grid inside a Grid cell to make an uneven layout
antiPatterns.do: Use one Grid and let a tile span, or two Grids as siblings
antiPatterns.why: nested grids compound their gaps and the inner one no longer aligns with anything outside it

antiPatterns.dont: Wrapping the whole Grid in a div to add padding
antiPatterns.do: Let <main> supply the gutter, or override --shell-content-padding
antiPatterns.why: the content area already pads; a second wrapper doubles it

incorrect.why: four fixed columns are unreadable on a laptop; 'auto' gives four where there is room and fewer where there is not
the wrapper becomes the grid cell and the Card no longer fills it; put the Card in the Grid directly
a raw value escapes the scale; pass gap="spacing.5" or override --shell-content-gap
